persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Brian, 19. You finished high school in Illinois last year and now work at your uncle's hardware store. You dream of becoming an electrician, but you do not know where to start, and the dream feels very far away. Today you want a clear picture of your future and one small step you can take this month.

challenge.intro: Now you are Brian. Compass is empty. Nobody will tell you which button to press. Use what you learned. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Open Daraja Compass with the normal app link. If the welcome tour shows, tap 'skip the tour' → '✨ Start fresh with my own' → OK. If it does not show, scroll to the very bottom of the page and tap '🧹 Start fresh — erase this app’s data' → OK → OK (if it says there is nothing to erase, just tap OK). If it asks 'Where are you?', tap USA. You should see the card 'Where are you going?' with the button 'Start my Compass →'.

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: helps you picture your life five years from now
walks backward from the dream to smaller goals
ends with one small step to do this month, and you tick it when done

subs: Visit the technical college to ask about the course
Visit the community college to ask about the course

lines: Welcome. This short video explains Daraja Compass. In about four minutes you will know what it is for and how to use it.
First, the problem. Many people have a dream. A trade. Their own small business. A good job, a home of their own. But the dream feels far away, and nobody shows them the first step.
So the years pass, and the dream stays a dream.
Compass helps you turn a dream into a plan. You answer fifteen plain questions about yourself and your future.
Then it writes a picture of your life five years from now, in your own words. And it helps you walk backward from that picture to one small step you can take this month.
Who is it for? A young person finishing school, a student, someone starting over. A parent or a mentor can sit beside them while they do it.
Let us look at the screen. At the top is the name, Daraja Compass. Your life, mapped by you.
Under it, a gold box says what Compass is for, in plain words.
The first card asks: Where are you going? Under it is a Bible verse that changes every day.
Tap Start my Compass to begin. It takes about ten minutes.
Now the questions come one at a time. At the top it says question one of fifteen, and a gold bar fills as you go.
The first questions are easy: your name, then your age. Type in the box, or tap the microphone and just talk.
Next saves your answer and moves on.
Many questions have example answers you can tap. Tap one and it goes into the box. Then change the words so they fit you.
Some questions are just a choice, like marriage in the next five years: Yes, Maybe, or Not in five years. Tap one. No typing.
Back goes to the question before. You can skip anything, and there are no wrong answers.
One question asks what monthly income would make that life possible. Compass uses that number later for some simple money math.
On the last question the button says Paint my picture.
Compass writes your five-year picture: your work, your money, your home, your faith, and how you help others.
If it is not right, tap Change answers. If it is the life you want, tap Yes, build my path.
Now the clever part. Compass walks backward from the dream. For each goal there are lines with a time in gold: five years, three years, two years, one year, six months, and this month.
On each line you write what has to be true by then. To be an electrician in five years, maybe in one year you must finish the course.
The last line, this month, matters most. One small step you can do in the next few weeks, with a date. Visit a college. Ask one question. Open a savings account.
Then tap Save my path, my Compass, and you arrive at your Compass home. At the top it counts Goals met.
The card called This month shows your small steps. When you finish one, tap its box. It turns green with a tick, and you get a star.
Every twenty-eight days, Compass asks how the month went. Tick what happened, move what slipped, and write next month's step.
The printer button at the top prints the screen you are on, handy for your five-year picture or your path.
Everything saves on this phone as you go. There is no account, and nothing is sent anywhere.
Daraja Compass is free.
And the question mark button in the corner has the tour and help any time you need them.
